guitar.notes: Hozier is commonly seen with Gibson acoustic guitars (e.g. J-45-style) live, and Telecasters for electric parts; reasonably documented but not singularly iconic.

tone.target: jangly edge-of-breakup indie clean with light chorus sheen
tone.profile: jangly edge-of-breakup indie clean with light chorus sheen
tone.summary: A bright, airy signal chain utilizing a light boost/OD for edge-of-breakup grit, followed by a classic Fender-style amp model (US Deluxe) paired with a 2x12 cab. Chorus adds the required sheen, and Room reverb provides subtle space.

rig.name: Hozier - Jackie and Wilson (guitar) - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Provide subtle, controlled boost to achieve the 'edge-of-breakup' sound without heavy distortion.
blocks.gap: The Boost module is used instead of a dedicated OD/Overdrive pedal to keep the tone transparent and chimey, matching the clean indie aesthetic.

blocks.purpose: Bypass or use a very subtle setting if needed for extra grit (kept off to maintain chime).
blocks.gap: The Boost module handles the necessary breakup. A dedicated OD pedal was avoided per instructions.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the bright, clean, Fender/Vox-style amp required for jangly arpeggios and airy top end.
Provide the compact, bright sound signature associated with smaller combo amps and 2x12 cabinets.
Add the required 'light modulation' and subtle sheen without sounding artificial.
Enhance the 'airy top end' and 'chime' while reducing any potential muddiness or roundness.
Provide the required 'small room reverb' and subtle sense of space.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism by swapping the default 2x12 IR for a more open, chimey speaker that better captures the required jangly arpeggios.

proposals.reason: Enhance chime and open top end for arpeggios.
